Kosher food in Cervinia, Milan and Turin

A guide for the independent traveller: what the village has and has not, which products in an Italian supermarket are kosher and under whose supervision, and where to stock up on the way.

Open the kosher guide in the full site
🏔️ In the village🛒 Supermarket products📦 Delivery🏙️ Milan🏛️ Turin💧 Mikveh

ℹ️ What is there in the village?

In Cervinia itself there are no kosher restaurants, no kosher bakeries and no synagogue.
The village has a small supermarket, Crai, with basic groceries.
At busy times Israelis on the spot often organise themselves — a minyan, a Shabbat meal, shared shopping. It is worth checking the Israeli Facebook group for Cervinia (in Hebrew) before the trip — the arrangements are posted there, and WhatsApp groups for particular dates usually start from there too.

💡 How to check a product in the supermarket
  • 📱 Scan the barcode at the shelf — the Bologna community maintains an online version of the Italian kashrut list: search by brand, browse by category, and barcode scanning with the camera. 1,471 products, about 690 of them with a photo. This is the most practical tool in the supermarket. Open the search → (the camera sends nothing anywhere)
  • 📋 The full official list — 92 pages, in Italian. PDF →
  • 🧳 Bringing food from home — allowed and recommended · 🛒 Stock up on the way — the village supermarket is small and expensive · 🔥 Most holiday apartments have a kitchen
🕍 One way to eat kosher in Cervinia: travel with a group

Fun Fit Family run kosher ski holidays in Cervinia — a whole hotel with a kosher kitchen, full board, equipment rental included, a separate children's programme with staff, and a traditional Shabbat on site. The hotel is Hotel Lo Stambecco at Plan Maison, at 2,550 m — ski-in/ski-out right on the slope. No road leads to it: the only access is by the lift from the village, which runs 8:30–16:30 and is free for guests, and outside those hours you can book a private snowmobile transfer. Plan your arrival time accordingly.
They have run such holidays since 2021, in Cervinia and in Pinzolo. The next date is Hanukkah, 6–13 December 2026.
Kashrut: a resident mashgiach, glatt meat and chalav Yisrael, unless stated otherwise.
What is included at Hanukkah, by their own announcement: kosher full board, ski equipment rental, a 5-day ski pass, kids' club and ski school, evening activities and entertainment, and group airport transfers. Price: from €1,800 per adult.
To book, for details and cancellation terms — contact them directly: WhatsApp +39 320 349 3380 or email info@funfit-fam.com.
Their website → · The hotel's website →

🛒 What you can buy in the supermarket in Cervinia and in Italy — with the certifying body

The list is based on "Prodotti approvati 5786-2026" of the Assembly of Italian Rabbis (ARI) with the support of UCEI. Each product shows its certifying body, so everyone can weigh the level of kashrut for themselves. The full list (PDF, 92 pages)

How to read the list 7
  • 🔤 The halachic status mark — P = pareve · L = dairy · fish = pareve but not to be eaten with meat.
  • 📦 "Symbol on pack" — where this is written, the product is kosher only if the kosher symbol is actually printed on the packet. The same brand without the symbol — not included.
    Where it is not written, the list can be relied on even without a symbol on the pack
  • 🏛️ "BDM/BDR approved" — checked and approved by the Milan and Rome batei din together with the certifying bodies. There is supervision, but no kosher symbol on the pack — the list is the only authority.
  • 🥛 Unsupervised milk — note. The list says explicitly that every dairy product not otherwise marked contains unsupervised milk (chalav akum / chalav stam), and its permission rests on the lenient view, among them Rabbi Moshe Feinstein. No product on the list is marked "chalav Yisrael".
    If you keep chalav Yisrael — none of the items marked L suits you, including the butter, the yoghurt, the ice cream and most of the chocolate
  • 🍞 Pat Yisrael — the list notes that a product not explicitly marked is not pat Yisrael. There is no fresh bread on the list at all.
  • ✡️ Mehadrin — the introduction says the list mixes different levels of kashrut and that mehadrin products are "marked in place". In practice, on the food pages no product carries a "mehadrin" mark. What is marked, on a few: yashan (Pasta di Camerino, Sgambaro), bishul Yisrael (Pizzoli frozen chips), and Badatz Beit Yosef (Dante olive oil).
    Rule of thumb: the level of kashrut is set by the certifying body listed by the product, not by its appearing on the list
  • 🏷️ The certifying bodies that appear hereOU · OK · Star-K · KLBD (London) · Kof-K · MK (Manchester Beth Din) · NWK (North West Kosher) · KF · 1K · KV · Euro Kosher · Milan Beth Din · Rome Beth Din · Badatz Shomrei Hadas (Antwerp) · Badatz Beit Yosef
    And individual rabbis, by name

Something else useful 2
  • 🔬 The list of forbidden food additives — at the end of the booklet there is a table by Rabbi Riccardo Di Segni, by European E numbers: which additives are always forbidden and which are forbidden without supervision. Useful when a product is not on the list and you want to read the label.
    Always forbidden: E120, E441, E542, E630, E631, E635, E1000 · may be of dairy origin: E469, E637, E966
  • ⚠️ The list is updated every year and during it too. It is meant for private use according to each person's level of kashrut, and does not replace asking a rabbi.

📦 Kosher4U — delivery of kosher products

A European delivery service for kosher food. Tested in practice — it was used for a delivery to Cervinia and the service worked. Order online and receive the delivery, without carrying food from home.
⚠️ Few use it for Italy. Make sure with them that the service is active for your destination before you build your plans on it.

💡 Order early, especially in peak season, and give the dates of your stay and the delivery address.

🛒 Another option: stock up in Milan on the way — see the "Milan" tab.

🏙️ Kosher food in Milan, on the way to Cervinia

🚗 Milan on the way to Cervinia — the real chance to stock up. All the kosher food is concentrated in the south-western quarter (Soderini · Sally Mayer · Washington · San Gimignano), not near the main synagogue.

🛒 What to buy in Milan for a stay in the village:
Tinned tuna · pasta and sauce · biscuits · sealed cheeses · juices · snacks for the lift
🍱 Catering: Chabad Milan works with Eshel Israel (glatt meat, under the Milan rabbinate), and the shops on Via Soderini and around it also sell ready-made and frozen food.
No official source publishes opening hours for these businesses. Phone before you go — hours shift around Shabbat, holidays and August.

🕍 Synagogues in Milan 10

Most of the kosher food and lodging is in the south-western quarter (Soderini · Sally Mayer · Montecuccoli · San Gimignano), and most of the synagogues too. Milan has no eruv, so the distance from your lodging to the synagogue matters.
The city has more small oratories — Centro Modena on Via Tenca and Josef Tehillot on Via dei Gracchi among others. The full list is on the community's website, mosaico-cem.it.

🕍 Chabad House of Milan

Via Luigi Soderini 3

Three minyanim a day, all year. No need to arrange in advance.
Weekdays: Shacharit 7:00, and a second minyan usually at 8:30 · Mincha 19:45 in summer / 13:30 in winter · Maariv 19:45 in winter.
Shabbat: Mincha and Kabbalat Shabbat — 19:15 in summer, and in winter at candle lighting · Shacharit 10:00 · Mincha an hour and twenty minutes before Shabbat ends.

Website · Map

The summer and winter schedule follows the clock change. Most of the kosher food and lodging is in this area too.

🛏️ Shabbat-friendly lodging in Milan 6

What matters is a mechanical key and no light sensors. The first on the list was checked in practice; the rest come from Metaylim BeKippa (metaylimbkipa.com), which states it explicitly for each property. Locks and lighting change — confirm with the hotel before you book. And Milan has no eruv.

💧 The nearest mikveh

Details and how to arrange

Nearest: Turin (Torino), about 120 km. Through the Jewish Community offices, by appointment: 📞 +39 011 650 8332 · segreteria@torinoebraica.it
